Do not reveal the implementation, new identifiers, exact code, patch syntax, file-and-line locations, or instructions for how to fix it. Return only the problem statement.

PR title:
Fix flag value set when is_flag=True and type is provided

PR body:
When setting the value of a flag, check only if `is_flag` is `True` and `flag_value` is not provided when negating the default flag value.

#2829 introduced a bug by checking if the type of the flag is `None` before setting the value.
Since we still check if `is_flag` is set, objects without a `__bool__` method will not raise an error if `is_flag` is not set.

fixes #2894
fixes #2897

Gold patch (use only to infer the symptom; do not quote or describe the fix):
diff --git a/CHANGES.rst b/CHANGES.rst
index f9f33ec0..6cdc25c5 100644
--- a/CHANGES.rst
+++ b/CHANGES.rst
@@ -3,6 +3,8 @@
 Version 8.2.1
 -------------
 
+-   Fix flag value handling for flag options with a provided type. :issue:`2894`
+    :issue:`2897` :pr:`2930`
 
 Version 8.2.0
 -------------
diff --git a/src/click/core.py b/src/click/core.py
index 4745b533..f57ada62 100644
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -2610,10 +2610,11 @@ class Option(Parameter):
             else:
                 self.default = False
 
+        if is_flag and flag_value is None:
+            flag_value = not self.default
+
         self.type: types.ParamType
         if is_flag and type is None:
-            if flag_value is None:
-                flag_value = not self.default
             # Re-guess the type from the flag value instead of the
             # default.
             self.type = types.convert_type(None, flag_value)

message.content: The bug causes flag options that specify a `type` to not set the correct flag value when the flag is used, resulting in the flag's value being incorrect or unset.
